RUN.about: Cut by the life of a document — an author creates and sends it, a recipient signs it, the system seals it — after which templates, org management, embedding, admin, and auth extend the core flow.

AUTHORED.detail: A background job decorates each PDF with signed fields, appends certificate and audit-log pages, digitally signs the result, and marks the envelope COMPLETED. A parallel CSC path handles qualified electronic signatures.

group.note: The seal job is the main path; CSC signing is an alternative transport; certificate generation and signing transports are shared infrastructure.

issues.title: Signer instance cached in module global
issues.detail: The `signer` variable in `signPdf` is set once and never cleared. If the P12 certificate expires or the GCloud HSM key rotates during a long-lived process, the stale signer continues to be used until restart.

issues.title: Sweep job marks retries as resealing
issues.detail: The sweep passes `isResealing: true` for documents that were never sealed at all (just missed the initial trigger). This forces the handler to use `initialData`, which may confuse audit semantics for first-time seals.

AUTHORED.sub: Sign up, sign in, OAuth, passkeys, two-factor authentication, sessions, profile, and security settings.
AUTHORED.detail: A Hono auth server handles all credential methods through a unified `onAuthorize` chokepoint that issues sessions. The Remix frontend provides unauthenticated sign-in/up routes and authenticated settings for profile and security.

children.sub: All authentication methods: email-password, Google, Microsoft, OIDC, passkeys, and organisation portals
children.detail: Every sign-in path calls `onAuthorize`, which checks the user is not disabled, mints a session token, and sets a signed cookie. Rate limiting, CSRF, and captcha validation happen per-route before credentials are checked.

issues.title: OAuth linking clears unverified user's password
issues.detail: When an OAuth account is linked to an existing unverified user, the password is set to null. If the user previously set a password via email signup, they lose their password credential silently upon first OAuth sign-in.

children.title: Security Middleware
children.sub: CSRF origin validation, CSP with per-request nonces, and security audit logging
children.detail: Three layers protect the app: Origin-based CSRF rejects cross-site mutations (except API-key requests), a per-request nonce feeds a strict-dynamic CSP with path-aware frame-ancestors, and all auth events are logged to `userSecurityAuditLog`.
